Empathy Health

Making the care people trust easier to see, understand and connect with.

I put together this concept to show how I would approach Empathy Health's online presence, family communication and the operational work behind it.

Explore the direction ↓

I looked at the business first

Before creating content, I wanted to understand what families are actually looking for.

Families aren't simply looking for "home care." They're looking for someone they can trust with a person they love.

  • Reassurance
  • Reliability
  • Dignity
  • Communication
  • Independence
  • Someone who follows through

So the content has to do more than describe services. It has to answer the question underneath every search: will my parent be okay?

The content direction

The goal isn't to post more.

It's to become easier to trust.

  1. 01

    Education

    Make home-care questions easier to understand.

  2. 02

    Family

    Speak to the emotions and realities families are already living.

  3. 03

    Caregivers

    Show the people behind the care.

  4. 04

    Community

    Build local relevance across Vancouver and surrounding communities.

  5. 05

    Trust

    Show what reliable, personalized care actually looks like.

The social feed

Posts that sound like the questions families already ask.

The idea

Give families a plain checklist for a conversation they've been putting off.

Why it works

It's easy to save and send to a sibling, which is often how this decision actually gets made.

The idea

Say the brand promise in five words, with a room that looks like someone's real home.

Why it works

It shows what home care feels like before anyone has to read about services.

The idea

Show the ordinary moment: a conversation over a meal.

Why it works

The caregiver is a person, not a uniform. That is the trust signal.

The carousel

One idea. Seven moments. One conversation.

The point isn't simply to educate.

It's to make someone recognize their own situation in the story.

Recognition→Emotion→Reassurance→Trust→Action

Reel concept

You can love your parents deeply and still not be able to do everything.

Reel concept

Some of the strongest content doesn't feel like advertising.

  1. An adult daughter checks her phone.
  2. She calls her parent.
  3. She works while thinking about home.
  4. She visits her parent.
  5. A caregiver provides support.
  6. The family spends time together.

Support doesn't replace family.
It gives family room to be family.

Beyond social media

And there's another side to the work.

The content gets attention.
The systems make sure nothing gets lost.

I have more than five years in customer success, administration and operations, including client communication, lead qualification and follow-up for a U.S.-based healthcare company.

Client communication

Clear, timely responses and follow-up.

Lead organization

Research, qualification, tracking and CRM updates.

Administrative support

Scheduling, documentation, coordination and task management.

Business development support

Research on referral partners, local organizations and the right contacts: senior and retirement communities, rehabilitation centres, hospitals and discharge planners, social workers, home health professionals and community groups.

Research→Organize→Communicate→Follow up→Track

I'd keep it in Airtable, Google Sheets or your CRM. I can't promise leads. I can build a clear process for finding and developing the right relationships.

The first 30 days

Start with understanding. Build from there.

  1. Week 01

    Understand

    Review existing social channels, content, audience, inquiries and workflows.

  2. Week 02

    Build

    Set content pillars, visual consistency, a content calendar and a tracking system.

  3. Week 03

    Publish and learn

    Begin consistent content, watch engagement and see what families respond to.

  4. Week 04

    Refine

    Review performance, sharpen the content direction and identify useful outreach and referral opportunities.

What you get from me

You don't just get someone to post.

You get someone who notices what needs to be done.

  • Content that sounds human.
  • A social presence built around trust.
  • Consistent content organization.
  • Client and lead follow-up.
  • Administrative support.
  • Research and relationship tracking.
  • Someone who communicates instead of disappearing.
  • Someone who looks for ways to make the workflow easier.

The goal isn't simply to post more.

It's to make Empathy Health's online presence feel as caring, credible and human as the service itself.

That's the kind of support I'd want to bring to the team: thoughtful content, reliable follow-through and someone who can take ownership of the details behind the work.
